data.name: Destiny of a Wizard
data.detailed_description:
THE STORY THUS FAR:

Since the dawn of time, the power of the Blue Wizards
has been known to all folk. Life was peaceful for many years until an evil being known as Darklin came into the realm of the Vale Islands

This was known as the "Darkest Hour".
Many perished...men...women...and children.
The battle between the powerful Blue Wizards and the
force known as Darklin waged on for many, many years. Until finally, the Wizards drove off Darklin and he was banished to another realm.

Even though he was defeated, he was not dead.

The Wizards sealed him away. The only way he could be brought back is by sacrificing a Wizard. By sacrificing a Wizard, their power could be used to release the powers of darkness.

This would break the seal that binds Darklin.
Knowing this knowledge, the Wizards decided to shut themselves away from everyone.

They decided to live in secret so that no force, good or evil, can know where the descendants of the Wizards lived.
Our story begins here, where the Wizards reside in peace and in secret....

FEATURES OF THE GAME:
* A linear turned based RPG spanning over five chapters.

* Old school style retro fast pace combat.

* Comedy references full of derpness including "4th wall" ones!

* Over 50 various monsters to do battle with!

* Experience voice overs from over six different characters that bring the game to life!

* Extra features including bloopers and commentary bonuses!

* Unlock magical spells as you seek out the four elemental crystals of the Vale Islands.

* A special hidden sixth chapter which includes several features not from the main adventure!

data.short_description: You are the descendant of the long forgotten Blue Wizards, who sealed an evil presence many years ago. Now a new threat has emerged and plans to release this presence into the world again!

reviews.review:
This was the developer's first game, and it shows.

The maps are really simple. The dungeons, vaguely reminiscent of Phantasy Star II in their monotony, are composed mostly of arbitrary pathways with repeating assets. Thematically speaking, a few dungeons took influence from the first Final Fantasy to the point of predictability. I found mermaids at the top of some underwater ruins while the boss was at the bottom. The world map was largely similar, although I really liked the idea behind the interconnected islands in the third portion of the game. They reminded me a lot of the Dezoris caves in the first Phantasy Star. The fourth area has almost nothing for the player to explore and I found this underwhelming, especially compared to the extras in the first part of the game. An optional dungeon early in the game is thematically disjointed, as the player is in a desert area and ends up surrounded by trees in an underground thief hideout. Destiny Of A Wizard advocates exploration and hidden items, but the end result is minimal. Money is eventually a formality, and found in chests late in the game with no reason to spend any of it. A dungeon early in the game horrendously overused random pitfalls, forcing the player to run through a dungeon many times. This idea returns in several dungeons, albeit with less aggravation behind it. Late in the game there is a tower with two pathways the player explores, with a switch at the top of either side. As someone who enjoys the many ideas one can use with tower dungeons, I found this part to be much more interesting than most other dungeons. I was reminded of Pazuzu's Tower in Final Fantasy Mystic Quest, but presented with a dungeon that was surprisingly less monotonous to explore. 

The opening scene of Destiny Of A Wizard is lifted directly out of Dragon Quest IV. The game's progression, ending and main plot points, are lifted directly from Final Fantasy Mystic Quest. Dialogue is riddled with awkward grammar, spelling errors, and dialogue cut off by a known (and easily remedied) issue with RPG Maker text boxes.

Status effects are used poorly, especially in the case of paralysis. Being hit with several effects at once. and being subsequently beaten to death with no ability to alter the situation, is poor design. Throughout the whole game the accessory slot in the equipment menu is not used. There is no way to protect yourself from any status effect and there are no accessories to strategize with. Most enemies in the game are simply stronger versions of everything the player encounters in the first hour, with few deviations. Everything is overused. For a game about magic and wizards, there is little incentive to use your magic until late in the game. By the time your first spells are available your regular attack does the same, if not more damage. The game quickly becomes nothing more than obsessively pressing the attack button and occasionally healing. There is no change until some buff and debuff abilities are introduced late into the game, several of which are necessary to beat unbalanced bosses who heal absurd amounts of HP every turn. The beginning of the game is mostly powering up to meet a staggering challenge, eventually tapering off to become negligible.

For whatever reason the player misses a lot early in the game. I suspect there are some accuracy problems with early game weapons, as the player's statistics do not appear to have any effect on accuracy. Most equipment throughout the game lowers the player's Agility, leaving most battles with the player being hit 1-3 times by every monster before taking one action. The player naturally wants better defense, but the inability to do anything in combat stultifies the upgrade. In the very beginning of the game it is possible for the player to buy one piece of equipment, leave their first battle in a crippled state, and be incapable of paying to rest at the inn. Being forced to start over, especially with the limited save points available, is not an inspiring experience.

Despite all this, a wholesome sense of humour permeates the game and I would have liked to see more of that. Many references to popular games, characters, movies, and other things are scattered throughout NPC interactions and the plot progression. This game has all the right pieces required to be a great entry-level RPG. I would encourage the creator to edit the project to be more user-friendly, and clean up the presentation of their ideas. The RPG genre needs games like this, not only to be welcoming to people unfamiliar or uncomfortable with the genre, but also to mitigate the negative reputation RPG Maker has as a whole. By creating a more refined experience, the path is laid for greater success and reception of the other two games the creator has made.
